summary: @whalent/agent-core ships obfuscated remote-controlled shell/PTY agent with self-upgrading runtime
details: The package's main bundle (dist/index.cjs, ~13.7 MB) is a remote-controlled host agent. It wires a WebSocket client to child_process/spawn and node-pty, framing messages as 'onData'/'heartbeat'/'register' with 'Authorization'/'token' auth, so data received from a remote WebSocket peer drives a shell/PTY on the machine running the package — a full-host command-execution channel. The README states the package is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades', and the bundle references 'upgrade', 'daemon', and '/api/' alongside the WebSocket/auth logic, providing an out-of-band code-replacement path that bypasses registry review: whatever the remote daemon serves becomes the code executing on the installer's host. The entire bundle is transformed with obfuscator.io (rotating string array of 105,701 entries, decoder wrappers like `_0xNNNN`, control-flow flattening); no HTTPS URL appears in plaintext despite the code making WebSocket, HTTP `/api/`, and Authorization-bearing requests, so every network destination is reconstructed at runtime and hidden from static inspection. Dependencies include `ssh2` and `node-pty`, consistent with the interactive-shell backdoor shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
